rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the prayer-neglecter as one who expects no reward for praying and fears no punishment for abandoning prayer.
rows.anchor: فروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : هو المصلي الذي إن صلى لم يرج لها ثوابا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says they delay their prayers beyond their appointed times.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا : الذين يؤخرونها عن أوقاتها

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim, in a report from al-Mughira, explains the lapse as wasting prayer time.
rows.anchor: وكذا روى المغيرة عن إبراهيم ، قال : ساهون بإضاعة الوقت

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says they fail to pray on time and do not complete bowing or prostration.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي العالية : لا يصلونها لمواقيتها ، ولا يتمون ركوعها ولا سجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the warning that later people abandoned prayer in Maryam supports the interpretation of neglecting its times.
rows.anchor: قلت : ويدل على هذا قوله تعالى : { فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة }

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Another report from Ibrahim describes someone who raises his head from prostration while turning his gaze aside.
rows.anchor: وروي عن إبراهيم أيضا : أنه الذي إذا سجد قام برأسه هكذا ملتفتا

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub interprets the lapse as failing to recite or remember God.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب : هو ألا يقرأ ولا يذكر الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah's reading has lāhūn, ‘heedless,’ in place of sāhūn.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله " الذين هم عن صلاتهم لاهون "

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains the verse as people who negligently postpone prayer until after its proper time; Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits this report.
rows.anchor: وقال سعد بن أبي وقاص : قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله :

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are hypocrites who leave prayer in private but perform it in public, as in 4:142.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا : هم المنافقون يتركون الصلاة سرا ، يصلونها علانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi takes the following description of people who show off as evidence that the prayer-neglecters are hypocrites.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أنها في المنافقين قوله : { الذين هم يراؤون }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had the verse said ‘heedless in their prayer,’ it would have described believers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن وهب عن مالك : قال ابن عباس : ولو قال في صلاتهم ساهون لكانت في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata praises the verse for saying ‘about their prayer’ rather than ‘in their prayer.’
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء : الحمد لله الذي قال { عن صلاتهم } ، ولم يقل في صلاتهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari distinguishes neglecting prayer through abandonment and indifference, characteristic of hypocrites or brazen sinners, from incidental distraction during prayer.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : أي فرق بين قوله : { عن صلاتهم } ، وبين قولك : في صلاتهم ؟ قلت : معنى " عن " أنهم ساهون عنها سهو ترك لها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes that distraction during prayer is nearly unavoidable even for Muslims, including the Prophet, so jurists discuss the prostration of forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : أي فرق بين قوله : { عن صلاتهم } ، وبين قولك : في صلاتهم ؟ قلت : معنى " عن "

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says avoiding forgetfulness is impossible; the Prophet and Companions forgot, while those who never forget fail to reflect on prayer and attend only to its count; prophetic lapses came from greater thoughts or satanic distraction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي : لأن السلامة من السهو محال ، وقد سها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاته والصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite presents prayer as worship while praying from fear; a sinner presents it as worship so people will say he prays.
rows.anchor: الرابعة- قوله تعالى : { الذين هم يراؤون } أي يري الناس أنه يصلي طاعة وهو يصلي تقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reality of riya is seeking worldly benefit through worship; its root motive is seeking status in people's hearts.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الرياء طلب ما في الدنيا بالعبادة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi lists four forms of riya: beautifying religious comportment (described as part of prophecy), ascetic clothing, pious-sounding speech, and displaying or beautifying worship to be seen.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : الرياء بإظهار الصلاة والصدقة ، أو بتحسين الصلاة لأجل رؤية الناس ، وذلك يطول ، وهذا دليله ، قاله ابن العربي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying states that God's obligatory duties should not be concealed; Qurtubi cites it to explain public performance of the obligations.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام :  " ولا غمة{[16475]} في فرائض الله "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing obligatory worship is not riya: obligations should be public as signs of Islam and to remove suspicion about neglect; optional worship is normally better concealed, but showing it to set an example is good.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون الرجل مرائيا بإظهار العمل الصالح إن كان فريضة ، فمن حق الفرائض الإعلان بها وتشهيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riya occurs when someone displays worship so that onlookers will praise him for piety.
rows.anchor: وإنما الرياء أن يقصد بالإظهار أن تراه الأعين ، فتثني عليه بالصلاح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A man saw someone prolonging a prostration of gratitude in the mosque and remarked that it would have been admirable had he done it at home, suspecting ostentation.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أنه رأى رجلا في المسجد قد سجد سجدة الشكر فأطالها ، فقال : ما أحسن هذا لو كان في بيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi points to his earlier discussion of the rule and reality of riya, including the verse on disclosing charity.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى هذا المعنى في سورة " البقرة "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، علي، مالك
rows.claim: The first reported sense is obligatory alms: al-Dahhak transmits it from Ibn Abbas, it is also reported from Ali, and Malik holds it; the referent is hypocrites withholding zakat.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه زكاة أموالهم . كذا روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس . وروى عن علي رضي الله عنه مثل ذلك ، وقاله مالك

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says the hypocrite performs prayer for show, does not regret missing it, and withholds the zakat God made obligatory; Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Aziz transmits the report.
rows.anchor: بن عبد العزيز عن مالك قال : بلغني أن قوله الله تعالى

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says that if prayer were hidden from hypocrites as zakat is hidden, they would not pray.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم : لو خفيت لهم الصلاة كما خفيت لهم الزكاة

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب، سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab and Said ibn al-Musayyib say maʿun means wealth in Quraysh usage.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن " الماعون " المال ، بلسان قريش

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas interpret maʿun as the household's useful items, such as an axe, pot, or fire.
rows.anchor: وقول ثالث : أنه اسم جامع لمنافع البيت كالفأس والقدر والنار وما أشبه ذلك ، قاله ابن مسعود ، وروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: الزجاج، أبو عبيد، المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj, Abu Ubayd, and al-Mubarrad say pre-Islamic maʿun covered anything useful, from an axe, pot, bucket, or fire striker to any benefit, great or small; al-Aʿsha's verse illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: الرابع : ذكر الزجاج وأبو عبيد والمبرد أن الماعون في الجاهلية كل ما فيه منفعة

rows.speaker: الزجاج، أبو عبيد، المبرد
rows.claim: These lexicographers say maʿun in Islam means obedience and zakat, citing al-Raʿi's poem about giving the due zakat from wealth.
rows.anchor: قالوا : والماعون في الإسلام : الطاعة والزكاة ، وأنشدوا قول الراعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another reported sense from Ibn Abbas is a borrowed item or loan.
rows.anchor: الخامس : أنه العارية ، وروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب، الكلبي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Kalbi interpret maʿun as all customary acts of kindness people exchange.
rows.anchor: قاله محمد بن كعب والكلبي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A seventh reported interpretation is water and pasture.
rows.anchor: السابع : أنه الماء والكلأ .

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says it can mean water alone, quoting an Arab speaker and a line about a cloud pouring forth water.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : سمعت بعض العرب يقول : الماعون : الماء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Umar interprets maʿun as withholding a due right.
rows.anchor: التاسع : أنه منع الحق ، قاله عبد الله بن عمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Abbas that maʿun is the yield from benefits of property, deriving from maʿn, ‘a little.’
rows.anchor: العاشر : أنه المستغل من منافع الأموال ، مأخوذ من المعن وهو القليل ، حكاه الطبري عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub derives maʿun from scarcity: maʿn means a little, as in the Arab expression ‘he has neither saʿna nor maʿna.’
rows.anchor: قال قطرب : أصل الماعون من القلة . والمعن : الشيء القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi explains that zakat, charity, and similar good deeds are called maʿun because they are a little portion of much.
rows.anchor: فسمى الله تعالى الزكاة والصدقة ونحوهما من المعروف ماعونا ؛ لأنه قليل من كثير

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari suggests maʿun derives from maʿuna, ‘help,’ with the alif replacing the final hāʾ.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : الماعون : أصله معونة ، والألف عوض من الهاء ؛ حكاه الجوهري

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi analyzes maʿun as a passive participle from ‘to help’; help supplies the force, tools, and means that make an undertaking possible.
rows.anchor: ابن العربي : الماعون : مفعول{[16481]} من أعان يعين ، والعون : هو الإمداد بالقوة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash cites a fluent Bedouin using maʿun for obedience and compliance, and supports this sense with a rajaz verse about camels submitting or giving.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر : أنه الطاعة والانقياد . حكى الأخفش عن أعرابي فصيح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha asks what may not be withheld; the Prophet names water, fire, and salt and describes great reward for sharing each, including water where it is scarce. Al-Thaʿlabi cites the report and Ibn Majah records it; Qurtubi says its chain is weak.
rows.anchor: لأن عائشة رضوان الله عليها قالت : قلت يا رسول الله ، ما الشيء الذي لا يحل منعه ؟ قال : ( الماء والنار والملح )

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi offers another possibility: maʿun is assistance that is easy to provide, but God has made its provision burdensome.
rows.anchor: الماوردي : ويحتمل أنه المعونة بما خف فعله ، وقد ثقله الله .

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says refusing any single item does not warrant woe; woe belongs to one who combines neglecting prayer, showing off, and stinginess with maʿun.
rows.anchor: وقيل لعكرمة مولى ابن عباس : من منع شيئا من المتاع كان له الويل ؟ فقال : لا ، ولكن من جمع ثلاثهن فله الويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers that the passage concerns hypocrites, who combine neglecting prayer, riya, and withholding wealth, as described in 4:142 and 9:54.
rows.anchor: قلت : كونها في المنافقين أشبه ، وبهم أخلق ؛ لأنهم جمعوا الأوصاف الثلاثة : ترك الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says a Muslim who displays only one of these traits incurs a corresponding share of blame, especially when withholding aid is obligatory as prayer is obligatory.
rows.anchor: ويبعد أن توجد من مسلم محقق ، وإن وجد بعضها فيلحقه جزء من التوبيخ ، وذلك في منع الماعون إذا تعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outside necessity, refusing ordinary assistance is blameworthy as a breach of good character.
rows.anchor: إنما يكون منعا قبيحا في المروءة في غير حال الضرورة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the sura is Meccan by consensus and has five verses.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بإجماع ، وهي خمس آيات .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the report of Ibn Abbas found in the two Sahih collections, Muhammad gathers his clans at al-Safa after the command to warn his closest kin, asks whether they would believe a warning of approaching cavalry, and warns of severe punishment; Abu Lahab curses him for summoning them, and the sura is revealed.
rows.anchor: في الصحيحين وغيرهما -واللفظ لمسلم- عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت ( " وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين "

rows.speaker: الحميدي وغيره
rows.claim: The added account says Abu Lahab's wife comes with a hand-sized stone, but God veils Muhammad from her sight so she sees only Abu Bakr; she threatens to strike Muhammad and recites a rhyme denouncing him.
rows.anchor: زاد الحميدي وغيره : فلما سمعت امرأته ما نزل في زوجها وفيها من القرآن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Quraysh abuse and satirize ‘Mudhammam’ while he is Muhammad, and marvels that God has diverted their harm from him.
rows.anchor: وكانت قريش إنما تسمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مذمما ، يسبونه ، وكان يقول :

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd reports that Abu Lahab asked what he would receive if he believed; when told he would receive what other Muslims receive, he rejected a religion that made him their equal, and the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن سبب نزولها ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد أن أبا لهب أتى النبي

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan says Abu Lahab repeatedly turned visiting delegations away by calling Muhammad a lying magician; when one group insisted on meeting him, Abu Lahab cursed him, Muhammad was saddened, and the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقول ثالث حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان قال : كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Abu Lahab tried to throw a stone at the Prophet, God prevented him, and this sura was revealed because of that prevention.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا لهب أراد أن يرمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر ، فمنعه الله من ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses tabbat as ‘lost.’
rows.anchor: ومعنى " تبت " : خسرت ، قاله قتادة .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses tabbat as ‘failed’ or ‘disappointed.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : خابت ، قاله ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata glosses tabbat as ‘went astray.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضلت ، قاله عطاء .

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr glosses tabbat as ‘perished.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : هلكت ، قاله ابن جبير .

rows.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
rows.claim: Yaman ibn Riʾab says tabbat means she was left empty of every good thing.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان بن رئاب : صفرت من كل خير .

rows.speaker: الأصمعي، أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi reports that after Uthman was killed, a voice recited a poem lamenting how people deserted him and saying ‘tabban’ of what they did; the verse illustrates the word's use.
rows.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه لما قتل عثمان رحمه الله سمع الناس هاتفا يقول :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hands are specified because people do most work with them: his hands were ruined, and he himself was ruined.
rows.anchor: وخص اليدين بالتباب ؛ لأن العمل أكثر ما يكون بهما ، أي خسرتا وخسر هو .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes ‘hands’ to mean Abu Lahab himself, since Arabic can use a part for the whole; Qurtubi links this to 22:10.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد باليدين نفسه . وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد ، كما قال الله تعالى : { بما قدمت يداك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi calls part-for-whole expression common Arabic usage, as in saying time's hand or calamities' hands struck someone, and cites a poet's ‘hand of disasters.’
rows.anchor: تقول : أصابته يد الدهر ، ويد الرزايا والمنايا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the first tabban is a curse or prayer for destruction and the second is a factual report, like ‘May God destroy him; he has perished.’
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : التب الأول دعاء ، والثاني خبر ، كما يقال : أهلكه الله وقد هلك .

rows.speaker: عبد الله، أُبي
rows.claim: Abdullah and Ubayy read the second clause as ‘and he has indeed perished.’
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله وأبي " وقد تب "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab's given name was Abd al-Uzza; he was the Prophet's paternal uncle. His wife, al-Awraʾ Umm Jamil, was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb's sister, and both were fiercely hostile to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وأبو لهب اسمه عبد العزى ، وهو ابن عبد المطلب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . وامرأته العوراء أم جميل

rows.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي
rows.claim: Tariq ibn Abd Allah al-Muharibi recalls hearing Muhammad preach at the market of Dhu al-Majaz while a man behind him bloodied his legs and called him a liar; bystanders identified that man as Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: قال طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي : إني بسوق ذي المجاز ، إذ أنا بإنسان يقول : " يا أيها الناس ، قولوا لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Lahab claimed Muhammad had bewitched people, contrasting their ordinary hunger with Muhammad's having fed them a sheep's thigh and quenched them with a large jug of milk.
rows.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو لهب : سحركم محمد ، إن أحدنا ليأكل الجذعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi rejects the claim that Allah's calling this pagan by a kunya proves that it is generally acceptable to give unbelievers kunyahs.
rows.anchor: وقد ظن قوم أن في هذا دليلا على تكنية المشرك ، وهو باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reason Allah used Abu Lahab's kunya rather than his given name is that the latter was Abd al-Uzza, and Allah does not ascribe servanthood in Scripture to an idol.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه كان اسمه عبد العزى ، والعزى : صنم ، ولم يضف الله في كتابه العبودية إلى صنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reason is that Abu Lahab was more widely known by his kunya than by his given name.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه ، فصرح بها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reason is that a given name is nobler than a kunya, so Allah lowered him to the lesser form; prophets are addressed by their names.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أن الاسم أشرف من الكنية ، فحطه الله عز وجل عن الأشرف إلى الأنقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth reason is that Allah makes him literally the father of the Flame by consigning him to it, fulfilling the ominous name and portent he chose for himself.
rows.anchor: الرابع : أن الله تعالى أراد أن يحقق نسبته ، بأن يدخله النار ، فيكون أبا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says his family called him Abu Lahab because his face glowed with beauty; God redirected them from flattering names such as Abu al-Nur and Abu al-Diya to the blameworthy ‘flame,’ then made the Fire his abode.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل : اسمه كنيته . فكان أهله يسمونه أبا لهب ، لتلهب وجهه وحسنه

rows.speaker: مجاهد، حميد، ابن كثير، ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Muhaysin read Abī Lahab with a still hāʾ; they all keep the hāʾ in dhāt lahab open to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وابن كثير وابن محيصن :{ أبي لهب } بإسكان الهاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when God created the Pen and commanded it to record what would exist, the decree ‘Perished the hands of Abu Lahab’ was among what it wrote.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما خلق الله عز وجل القلم قال له : اكتب ما هو كائن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Asked by Mansur whether Abu Lahab could have escaped the Fire if his fate was in the Preserved Record, Hasan says he could not; it was written before Abu Lahab and his parents were created.
rows.anchor: وقال منصور : سئل الحسن عن قوله تعالى : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } ، هل كان في أم الكتاب ؟

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Adam-and-Moses report, Moses reproaches Adam for leading people from Paradise; Adam replies that God had written the matter before creating the heavens and earth, and the Prophet says Adam prevailed over Moses.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " فحج آدم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In Hammam's report from Abu Hurayra, Adam says Moses found in the Torah that it was written two thousand years before Adam's creation that Adam would disobey his Lord and go astray; Adam asks why Moses blames him for a prewritten act.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث همام عن أبي هريرة أن آدم قال لموسى : " بكم وجدت الله كتب التوراة قبل أن يخلقني ؟

rows.speaker: طاووس، ابن هرمز، الأعرج، أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report through Tawus, Ibn Hurmuz, and al-Aʿraj from Abu Hurayra gives a different interval: the Torah's writing preceded creation by forty years.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث طاووس وابن هرمز والأعرج عن أبي هريرة : ( بأربعين عاما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth and what he acquired in status could not ward God's punishment from him.
rows.anchor: أي ما دفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال ، ولا ما كسب من جاه .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets what he earned as his children, since a man's child is his earning.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : من الولد ، وولد الرجل من كسبه .

rows.speaker: الأعمش، ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ‘wa-ma-ktasaba’ (‘and what he acquired’), transmitting this reading from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش " وما اكتسب " ورواه عن ابن مسعود .

rows.speaker: أبو الطفيل
rows.claim: Abu al-Tufayl recounts that when Abu Lahab's sons fought before Ibn Abbas, one pushed him as he tried to separate them; Ibn Abbas angrily called them ‘evil earnings,’ meaning his children.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الطفيل : جاء بنو أبي لهب يختصمون عند ابن عباس ، فاقتتلوا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the best food a man eats is from his own earning, and his child is part of his earning; Abu Dawud records it.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " إن أطيب ما أكل الرجل من كسبه ، وإن ولده من كسبه "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Muhammad warned his clan of the Fire, Abu Lahab said he would ransom himself with his wealth and children if his nephew was right; this verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : لما أنذر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشيرته بالنار ، قال أبو لهب : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ma may be a negation (‘his wealth did not avail him’) or an interrogative (‘what did his wealth avail him?’).
rows.anchor: و " ما " في قوله : { ما أغنى } : يجوز أن تكون نفيا ، ويجوز أن تكون استفهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second ma may be a relative pronoun (‘what he earned’) or, with the verb, a verbal noun (‘his earning’).
rows.anchor: و " ما " الثانية : يجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي ، ويجوز أن تكون مع الفعل مصدرا
